selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What can happen to a person’s mind when it gets busy only with sin, carelessness, or just the physical world?
questions.answer: It can become small and unable to understand big truth.

questions.question: What makes some minds narrow in this passage?
questions.answer: Forgetting Allah, doing sins, and focusing only on material things.

questions.question: Why can’t such a person understand the biggest faith questions?
questions.answer: Because those questions are too wide and deep for a cramped mind.

questions.question: When unbelief is compared with belief, which one matches reason better?
questions.answer: Belief matches reason better.

questions.question: If they could truly see their unbelief, what would they find inside it?
questions.answer: A lot of nonsense and impossibility.

questions.question: What would careful thinking show them about unbelief?
questions.answer: It would show them that unbelief holds many impossible ideas.

questions.question: What is another very foolish choice mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: A person may even deny his own existence and the world’s existence.

questions.question: Why is that path unreasonable?
questions.answer: Because it puts what belongs to Allah onto countless weak created things.

questions.question: How do these truths enter a person properly?
questions.answer: Through full acceptance and humble surrender.

questions.question: How do the truths of belief come into a person?
questions.answer: By strong acceptance and willing surrender.

questions.question: What is this part mainly warning about?
questions.answer: It warns about falling into unbelief because of narrow thinking.

questions.question: What three things can trap a person’s understanding and make it too narrow?
questions.answer: Neglecting Allah, sin, and being stuck only on material things.

questions.question: What mistake do people make when they trust their little bit of knowledge too much?
questions.answer: They become proud and start denying.

questions.question: What is wrong with their minds and hearts in the passage?
questions.answer: Their minds are cramped, and their hearts are corrupted and spiritually dead.

questions.question: What happens to people with dried-up minds and dead hearts?
questions.answer: They fall into unbelief and go astray.

questions.question: What example is given about a person who refuses Allah’s necessary and eternal being and His perfect qualities?
questions.answer: He may wrongly spread those special qualities across countless beings or atoms.

questions.question: If someone rejects Allah’s greatness because it seems too grand, what wrong path might he take?
questions.answer: He might give Allah’s special qualities to endless created things.

questions.question: What do these truths escape from?
questions.answer: They escape absurd ideas, false tales, and dark ignorance.

questions.question: In what kind of hearts do these truths settle?
questions.answer: In healthy hearts.

questions.question: What two places are ready to receive these truths?
questions.answer: Good hearts and straight minds.

questions.question: What is the “Second Abyss” about in this passage?
questions.answer: It is about the danger of slipping into unbelief and misguidance.

questions.question: What kind of matters are described as too great for that shrunken understanding?
questions.answer: Lofty, huge, and endless matters.

questions.question: What do these people do because of pride in their limited knowledge?
questions.answer: They hurry to reject what is beyond them.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the size of faith questions?
questions.answer: They are very broad, deep, and all-encompassing.
